hed: Trump calls SCOTUS mail-ballot stay denial a ‘big loss,’ criticizes his appointees
dek: President Trump posted on Truth Social Tuesday blasting Monday night’s Supreme Court denial of a stay (No. 26A305) that left Judge Indira Talwani’s injunction on the USPS “Ballot Mail for Federal Elections” rule in place for the Nov. 2026 midterms. He called the unsigned order a “big loss for Republicans,” said mail-in voting is a “Nation Destroying SCAM,” praised dissenting Justices Alito and Thomas as “legends,” and said his appointees Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, and Barrett are “not the people I interviewed” and “merely a shell of their original selves.” Justice Kavanaugh’s concurrence left open a fair prospect the rule is within USPS authority but said midterms implementation would be arbitrary and capricious for lack of time.

byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: CNBC’s Tuesday write-through, CNN Politics’ “shells” wrap, and ABC News’ AP wire cast Trump’s Truth Social blast as escalating pressure on the Court after an implied 7–2 stay denial — noting his first-term appointees did not join Alito and Thomas, that roughly a third of votes are cast by mail, and that Brookings’ 2025 review found mail-ballot fraud extremely rare — while states already mailing under prior rules keep those processes for November.

cr.body: Fox News’ Tuesday reaction report, Just the News’ “fumes” write-through, and the Washington Examiner’s White House piece frame the post as Trump backing Alito–Thomas and attacking a Court he says delayed until it was “too late” to fix mail voting — while highlighting Kavanaugh’s concurrence that the USPS rule may yet fall within statutory authority later, and Trump’s praise of the dissenters as “legends” after a stay loss he ties to midterms integrity.
